text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- The reserves of Romania's central bank (BNR) might rise to $2.0 billion in July, BNR governor Mugur Isarescu said.
- The International Monetary Fund Board is expected to discuss resumption of credits to Romania on Tuesday.
- The Mobil Rom consortium led by France Telecom launched Romania's second GSM mobile telephone system.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Liquidation of private banks Dacia Felix and Credit Bank is imminent, the paper says.
- Exporters are worried over the appreciation and stability of the leu currency, saying its current exchange rates is preventing exports.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania's air force will use soon an upgraded version of the Soviet-made MiG-21 jet fighter, compatible with NATO standards, the paper says.
- The slow pace of privatisation in the energy sector has a negative impact on Renel SA electricity authority's economic performance, the paper says.
General
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Romania's Foreign Minister Adrian Severin has started a visit to the United States in a bid to persuade U.S. officials that Romania is ready to afford costs related to a possible integration in NATO, the paper says.
- French Defence Minister Charles Millon cancelled his visit to Romania, the paper says.
- The Defence Ministry will use around one third of its 1997 budget for investments, Defence Minister Victor Babiuc said.
ADEVARUL

- The Romanian and Hungarian defence ministers asked their German and French counterparts to support plans to create a joint Romanian- Hungarian peacekeeping force patterned on the French-German model.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
